title: candidate-feedback-draft-gabriel-cho-2026-03-31
content:
DRAFT NOTES - candidate: Gabriel Cho (Backend SRE/SDE-II) - onsite 2026-03-30
Owner: Taylor Reed
Interviewers: Priya Desai (system design), Aaron Brooks (coding), Maya Thompson (behavioral + product)

Quick summary / TL;DR:
- Strong pragmatic product sense and cross-team communication.
- Decent fundamentals but coding execution was shaky under time pressure (bug in traversal, missed simple hashmap optimization).
- System design answers were high-level and thoughtful but lacked concrete operational details (metrics/SLAs, capacity planning, failure modes).
- Recommendation: hold — not confident for SDE-II IC path as-is. Consider SDE-I or a follow-up take-home focused on performance/debugging.

Scores (quick, 1-5):
- Role fit: 3.5
- Technical (coding): 2.5
- System design: 3.0
- Behavioral/collab: 4.0
- Overall hire: 3.0 (no hire for SDE-II right now)

Detailed notes:
1) Coding (Aaron)
- Prompt: implement a streaming parser + sliding-window aggregator (similar to streaming metrics aggregator).
- Gabriel wrote a clear approach (two-pass idea) then implemented in Python during the session.
- Key issues: off-by-one bug in window boundaries, O(N^2) behavior for worst-case due to nested loops (didn't suggest hashmap or deque sliding-window pattern).
- Time management: spent ~20-25 min on correctness and ~10 min on optimizing; when pushed for complexity he proposed micro-optimizations rather than algorithm change.
- Strengths: explains tradeoffs well, tests a few edge cases manually.
- Weaknesses: misses standard sliding-window idiom, shows weaker fluency in algorithmic patterns under pressure.
- Follow-up suggestion: small take-home where he must optimize an existing naive implementation and submit complexity analysis + perf numbers.

2) System design (Priya)
- Prompt: design a low-latency feature-flag evaluation service at scale (100k qps, ttl-based caches, multi-region).
- Gabriel sketched a sensible architecture: API gateway -> stateless evaluators -> feature store (primary + replica) + CDN cache.
- Lacking specifics: did not define SLAs, SLOs, or how KV cache invalidation works across regions; didn't discuss consistent hashing vs sticky routing tradeoffs; limited discussion on monotonic rollout strategies and observability signals to detect regressions.
- Good: considered rollout safety, mentioned canarying and percentage rollouts. Gave examples of production incidents he handled (brief).
- Suggestion: probe with follow-ups on cache invalidation and partition tolerance next debrief if we care about infra depth.

3) Behavioral / cross-team (Maya)
- Very strong. Concrete examples of shipping features with product teams, prioritizing reliability vs speed, communicating incidents to PMs and execs.
- Culture: wants ownership, asks good clarifying questions, seems coachable.

Red flags / unknowns:
- No recent work building high-throughput systems (most recent was 20-30k qps service at previous company — need verification).
- Lacks strong infra SRE toolset examples (e.g., limited talk about Prometheus histograms/latency p99 tradeoffs).
- Coding under pressure is a concern for IC2+/SDE-II interview bar.

Recommendation and next steps:
- Not advancing to hire for SDE-II today.
- Options: (A) offer SDE-I / L3 role if team is open and comp expectations align; (B) ask for a focused take-home that evaluates algorithmic fluency and performance debugging (2-4 hour task); (C) if higher infra depth is required, invite for a targeted infra interview with SRE lead (Priya can run).
- If proceeding with take-home, checklist for evaluation: correctness, complexity improvement (≥ 2x), clear write-up of tradeoffs, and simple perf numbers (wall time for 1M events).

Action items (who):
- Taylor: consolidate notes and draft GH feedback entry (today).
- Priya: if we want infra follow-up, send targeted questions and availability (by EOD Fri).
- Aaron: prepare take-home template and scoring rubric (points for algorithmic improvement + perf).

Misc / TODOs:
- Add transcript/recording link to GH comments (Recording: https://redwood.zoom.us/rec/share/abcd-1234).
- Confirm salary expectations (candidate said expecting 180-200k base; need to confirm total comp range).
- Quick reference check if we decide to progress.

Notes to self:
- Keep feedback factual and example-driven in GH. Avoid subjective phrasing like "didn't seem confident"; instead cite concrete misses (sliding-window algorithm omitted).
- This doc is rough — will tidy before adding to Greenhouse.

End draft.
